shown with `ls -la`. *([Ch 2](docs/01-foundations/ch02-linux.md))* - **High Availability (HA)** — Redundancy so a service stays accessible if a component fails. *([Ch 1](docs/01-foundations/ch01-cloud-devops-fundamentals.md))* - **Horizontal scaling (scale out)** — Adding more machines, typically behind a load balancer. *([Ch 1](docs/01-foundations/ch01-cloud-devops-fundamentals.md))* - **Host-based routing** — Routing by hostname. *([Ch 14](docs/04-aws/ch14-load-balancing-scaling.md))* - **Host-based routing (Ingress)** — Routing by hostname to different Services. *([Ch 20](docs/05-kubernetes/ch20-kubernetes-networking-scaling.md))* - **Hosted zone** — Route 53 container of DNS records for a domain (public or private). *([Ch 16](docs/04-aws/ch16-route53-cloudfront-waf.md))* - **Host Physical Address (HPA)** — Actual RAM location; GVA → GPA → HPA is the VM memory translation chain. *([Ch 36](docs/01-foundations/ch36-virtualization-internals.md))* - **Hot partition** — One DynamoDB key receiving disproportionate traffic. *([Ch 33](docs/04-aws/ch33-advanced-aws-backend.md))* - **HPA** — Horizontal Pod Autoscaler: adjusts replica count from metrics. *([Ch 20](docs/05-kubernetes/ch20-kubernetes-networking-scaling.md))* - **HTTP** — Hypertext Transfer Protocol; application-layer web protocol. *([Ch 4](docs/01-foundations/ch04-networking.md))* - **HTTPS** — HTTP over TLS. *([Ch 4](docs/01-foundations/ch04-networking.md))* - **HTTP to HTTPS redirect** — Redirecting :80 requests to :443. *([Ch 16](docs/04-aws/ch16-route53-cloudfront-waf.md))* - **Hybrid cloud** — Private infrastructure combined with public cloud (e.g. via VPN). *([Ch 1](docs/01-foundations/ch01-cloud-devops-fundamentals.md))* - **Hypervisor** — The virtualization layer that creates and manages VMs and controls their access to physical resources. *([Ch 36](docs/01-foundations/ch36-virtualization-internals.md))*

title: Glossary
heading: I
text: - **IaaS** — Infrastructure as a Service: rent infrastructure; you manage OS, runtime, app (e.g. EC2). *([Ch 1](docs/01-foundations/ch01-cloud-devops-fundamentals.md))* - **IAM** — Identity and Access Management: who are you and what may you do. *([Ch 9](docs/04-aws/ch09-aws-fundamentals-iam.md))* - **IAM group** — Collection of users sharing attached policies. *([Ch 9](docs/04-aws/ch09-aws-fundamentals-iam.md))* - **IAM policy** — JSON document defining allowed/denied actions on resources. *([Ch 9](docs/04-aws/ch09-aws-fundamentals-iam.md))* - **IAM role** — Identity assumable by trusted entities, giving temporary credentials. *([Ch 9](docs/04-aws/ch09-aws-fundamentals-iam.md))* - **IAM user** — Identity representing a person/persistent identity in an account. *([Ch 9](docs/04-aws/ch09-aws-fundamentals-iam.md))* - **Idempotency** — Processing the same message more than once has the same effect as once. *([Ch 15](docs/04-aws/ch15-lambda-serverless-messaging.md))* - **Idempotency (Ansible)** — Re-running yields the same state without unnecessary changes. *([Ch 28](docs/06-iac-config/ch28-ansible.md))* - **Idempotency-Key** — Client-supplied key letting servers deduplicate retried requests. *([Ch 22](docs/07-observability-sre/ch22-observability-reliability.md))* - **Idempotency-Key header** — Client-supplied key letting the API return the existing order for retried POST /orders. *([Ch 35](docs/08-production/ch35-devops-capstone.md))* - **ignore_changes** — Lifecycle setting ignoring changes to listed attributes. *([Ch 32](docs/06-iac-config/ch32-advanced-terraform.md))* - **Image (Docker)** — Immutable packaged template used to create containers. *([Ch 7](docs/02-containers/ch07-docker-fundamentals.md))* - **ImagePullBackOff / ErrImagePull** — Pod states where the container image cannot be pulled. *([Ch 18](docs/05-kubernetes/ch18-kubernetes-fundamentals.md))* - **Image scanning** — Vulnerability scanning of images for CVEs in OS packages and dependencies. *([Ch 8](docs/02-containers/ch08-docker-production.md))* - **Immutable image tag** — Unique per-version tag (e.g. commit SHA) instead of mutable `latest`. *([Ch 6](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch06-cicd-github-actions.md))* - **Immutable infrastructure** — Replace rather than patch: build a new version and swap out the old. *([Ch 8](docs/02-containers/ch08-docker-production.md))* - **Implicit dependency** - Dependency inferred from references between resources. *([Ch 21](docs/06-iac-config/ch21-terraform.md))* - Dependency inferred from attribute references. *([Ch 32](docs/06-iac-config/ch32-advanced-terraform.md))* - **Import block** — Declarative Terraform >=1.5 way to import existing resources. *([Ch 32](docs/06-iac-config/ch32-advanced-terraform.md))* - **Incident response** — Structured process from alert to mitigation and root-cause analysis. *([Ch 22](docs/07-observability-sre/ch22-observability-reliability.md))* - **Infrastructure as Code (IaC)** — Describing infrastructure in code so it can be reviewed, versioned and reproduced (e.g. Terraform). *([Ch 1](docs/01-foundations/ch01-cloud-devops-fundamentals.md))* - **Ingress** — Kubernetes object defining HTTP/HTTPS routing rules into the cluster. *([Ch 20](docs/05-kubernetes/ch20-kubernetes-networking-scaling.md))* - **Ingress Controller** — Component that implements Ingress rules (NGINX, AWS Load Balancer Controller, Traefik). *([Ch 20](docs/05-kubernetes/ch20-kubernetes-networking-scaling.md))* - **Inspector** — Vulnerability scanning service (awareness). *([Ch 17](docs/04-aws/ch17-monitoring-security.md))* - **Instance metadata (IMDS)** — Service exposing instance info and role credentials to the instance; use IMDSv2. *([Ch 10](docs/04-aws/ch10-ec2-compute.md))* - **Instance profile / EC2 IAM role** — Role attached to an instance providing temporary credentials. *([Ch 10](docs/04-aws/ch10-ec2-compute.md))* - **Instance type** — Hardware profile (vCPU, RAM, network) of an instance; grouped in families. *([Ch 10](docs/04-aws/ch10-ec2-compute.md))* - **Intel VT-x / AMD-V** — The CPU virtualization extensions of Intel and AMD. *([Ch 36](docs/01-foundations/ch36-virtualization-internals.md))* - **Interface endpoint** — VPC endpoint using private network interfaces for many AWS services. *([Ch 12](docs/04-aws/ch12-vpc-networking.md))* - **Internal module** — Company-standard reusable module built by a platform team. *([Ch 32](docs/06-iac-config/ch32-advanced-terraform.md))* - **Internet Gateway (IGW)** — VPC component providing Internet connectivity when routes point to it. *([Ch 12](docs/04-aws/ch12-vpc-networking.md))* - **Inventory (Ansible)** — List of hosts and groups Ansible manages. *([Ch 28](docs/06-iac-config/ch28-ansible.md))* - **IOPS** — Input/Output Operations Per Second of storage. *([Ch 13](docs/04-aws/ch13-rds-databases.md))* - **I/O virtualization** — Mediation of VM disk/network I/O by the hypervisor, reduced in overhead by VirtIO, SR-IOV and hardware assist. *([Ch 36](docs/01-foundations/ch36-virtualization-internals.md))* - **IP address** — Identifies a network interface at the IP layer (IPv4 32-bit, IPv6 128-bit). *([Ch 4](docs/01-foundations/ch04-networking.md))* - **IRSA** — IAM Roles for Service Accounts: Pod AWS permissions via OIDC and a ServiceAccount. *([Ch 31](docs/05-kubernetes/ch31-advanced-eks.md))* - **Istio** — Popular service mesh using Envoy proxies and the istiod control plane. *([Ch 30](docs/05-kubernetes/ch30-service-mesh-istio.md))* - **istiod** — Istio control-plane component configuring proxies. *([Ch 30](docs/05-kubernetes/ch30-service-mesh-istio.md))* - **Istio Gateway** — Istio ingress/egress entry point (not a Kubernetes Service). *([Ch 30](docs/05-kubernetes/ch30-service-mesh-istio.md))*

title: Glossary
heading: J
text: - **Jenkins** — Open-source general-purpose automation server for CI/CD pipelines. *([Ch 27](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch27-jenkins-advanced-cicd.md))* - **Jenkins agent** — Machine/pod that executes pipeline work. *([Ch 27](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch27-jenkins-advanced-cicd.md))* - **Jenkins controller** — Central Jenkins component managing jobs, scheduling, configuration, credentials and agents. *([Ch 27](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch27-jenkins-advanced-cicd.md))* - **Jenkins credentials store** — Secure storage of secrets injected via withCredentials. *([Ch 27](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch27-jenkins-advanced-cicd.md))* - **Jenkinsfile** — Pipeline-as-code file stored in the repository. *([Ch 27](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch27-jenkins-advanced-cicd.md))* - **Jenkins plugin** — Extension integrating Jenkins with other tools. *([Ch 27](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch27-jenkins-advanced-cicd.md))* - **Jitter** — Randomness added to retry delays to avoid synchronized retries. *([Ch 22](docs/07-observability-sre/ch22-observability-reliability.md))* - **Job** - A unit of a workflow that runs on a runner; independent jobs run in parallel. *([Ch 6](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch06-cicd-github-actions.md))* - Kubernetes object running a task to completion. *([Ch 20](docs/05-kubernetes/ch20-kubernetes-networking-scaling.md))* - **journalctl** — Command to read systemd journal logs (`-u` unit, `-f` follow). *([Ch 2](docs/01-foundations/ch02-linux.md))* - **JWT** — JSON Web Token used for stateless authentication. *([Ch 14](docs/04-aws/ch14-load-balancing-scaling.md))*

title: Glossary
heading: K
text: - **k6** — Load-testing tool using JavaScript scripts. *([Ch 34](docs/07-observability-sre/ch34-advanced-sre.md))* - **Karpenter** - Node provisioning/autoscaling tool for Kubernetes (EKS). *([Ch 20](docs/05-kubernetes/ch20-kubernetes-networking-scaling.md))* - Node provisioner that launches appropriate capacity for pending Pods. *([Ch 31](docs/05-kubernetes/ch31-advanced-eks.md))* - **KEDA** — Kubernetes Event-driven Autoscaling; scales workloads from queue depth etc. *([Ch 35](docs/08-production/ch35-devops-capstone.md))* - **Kernel** — Core of the OS; manages CPU, memory, processes, filesystems, networking, hardware, system calls. *([Ch 2](docs/01-foundations/ch02-linux.md))* - **Key pair** — Public/private SSH keys; private key stays with you, public key on the instance. *([Ch 10](docs/04-aws/ch10-ec2-compute.md))* - **kind** — Kubernetes in Docker: local clusters whose nodes are containers. *([Ch 18](docs/05-kubernetes/ch18-kubernetes-fundamentals.md))* - **KMS** - AWS Key Management Service for encryption keys. *([Ch 13](docs/04-aws/ch13-rds-databases.md))* - Key Management Service for cryptographic keys. *([Ch 17](docs/04-aws/ch17-monitoring-security.md))* - **Kubebuilder** — Framework for building Kubernetes operators in Go. *([Ch 29](docs/05-kubernetes/ch29-crds-operators.md))* - **kubectl** — Command-line tool for the Kubernetes API. *([Ch 18](docs/05-kubernetes/ch18-kubernetes-fundamentals.md))* - **kubectl api-resources** — Lists resource types available in the cluster including CRDs. *([Ch 29](docs/05-kubernetes/ch29-crds-operators.md))* - **kubectl auth can-i** — Checks whether an identity is permitted an action. *([Ch 29](docs/05-kubernetes/ch29-crds-operators.md))* - **kubectl logs --previous** — Show logs of the previous (crashed) container instance. *([Ch 20](docs/05-kubernetes/ch20-kubernetes-networking-scaling.md))* - **kubectl top** — Shows CPU/memory usage of Pods or nodes (needs Metrics Server). *([Ch 23](docs/08-production/ch23-production-architecture-troubleshooting.md))* - **kubelet** — Node agent ensuring assigned Pods are running. *([Ch 18](docs/05-kubernetes/ch18-kubernetes-fundamentals.md))* - **Kubernetes** — Container orchestration platform managing containers across a cluster. *([Ch 18](docs/05-kubernetes/ch18-kubernetes-fundamentals.md))* - **Kubernetes DNS** — Cluster DNS resolving Service names to Service IPs. *([Ch 20](docs/05-kubernetes/ch20-kubernetes-networking-scaling.md))* - **Kubernetes RBAC** — Authorization of access to Kubernetes API resources. *([Ch 31](docs/05-kubernetes/ch31-advanced-eks.md))*

title: Glossary
heading: L
text: - **Label** — Key-value metadata on Kubernetes objects. *([Ch 18](docs/05-kubernetes/ch18-kubernetes-fundamentals.md))* - **Lambda** — AWS serverless compute service running functions in response to events. *([Ch 15](docs/04-aws/ch15-lambda-serverless-messaging.md))* - **Lambda concurrency** — Number of simultaneous function executions. *([Ch 15](docs/04-aws/ch15-lambda-serverless-messaging.md))* - **Lambda event** — Input payload describing what triggered the function. *([Ch 15](docs/04-aws/ch15-lambda-serverless-messaging.md))* - **Lambda layer** — Shared package of libraries/dependencies attached to functions. *([Ch 15](docs/04-aws/ch15-lambda-serverless-messaging.md))* - **Latency budget** — Allocation of a total latency target across components. *([Ch 34](docs/07-observability-sre/ch34-advanced-sre.md))* - **Launch template** — Definition of the instance configuration an ASG launches. *([Ch 14](docs/04-aws/ch14-load-balancing-scaling.md))* - **Layer-by-layer troubleshooting** — Checking DNS/TLS, edge, LB, Kubernetes, app, dependencies in order. *([Ch 23](docs/08-production/ch23-production-architecture-troubleshooting.md))* - **Layer caching** — Docker reusing unchanged layers; depends on instruction ordering. *([Ch 8](docs/02-containers/ch08-docker-production.md))* - **Layer (Docker)** — Cacheable filesystem layer produced by a Dockerfile instruction. *([Ch 7](docs/02-containers/ch07-docker-fundamentals.md))* - **Leaky bucket** — Rate-limiting algorithm smoothing traffic to a constant outflow. *([Ch 34](docs/07-observability-sre/ch34-advanced-sre.md))* - **Least connections** — Algorithm sending traffic to the server with fewest active connections. *([Ch 4](docs/01-foundations/ch04-networking.md))* - **Least outstanding requests** — LB algorithm sending to the target with fewest in-flight requests. *([Ch 14](docs/04-aws/ch14-load-balancing-scaling.md))* - **Least privilege** — Grant only the permissions that are required. *([Ch 9](docs/04-aws/ch09-aws-fundamentals-iam.md))* - **Lifecycle policy** — Rules to transition objects between classes or expire them. *([Ch 11](docs/04-aws/ch11-s3-storage.md))* - **Linting** — Static checks for code-quality problems. *([Ch 6](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch06-cicd-github-actions.md))* - **Linux distribution** — Kernel packaged with utilities/software (Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora, Arch, Amazon Linux, RHEL). *([Ch 2](docs/01-foundations/ch02-linux.md))* - **Listener** — ALB component waiting for traffic on a port/protocol and forwarding per rules. *([Ch 14](docs/04-aws/ch14-load-balancing-scaling.md))* - **Little's Law** — L = lambda x W: average items in system = arrival rate x average time in system. *([Ch 34](docs/07-observability-sre/ch34-advanced-sre.md))* - **Live migration** — Moving a running VM between physical hosts by copying memory/state while it runs, then a brief pause to finish. *([Ch 36](docs/01-foundations/ch36-virtualization-internals.md))* - **Liveness** — Is the application still alive? *([Ch 8](docs/02-containers/ch08-docker-production.md))* - **Liveness probe** — Check deciding whether to restart a container. *([Ch 19](docs/05-kubernetes/ch19-kubernetes-config-storage.md))* - **Load balancer** — Distributes requests across backend servers; does health checks. *([Ch 4](docs/01-foundations/ch04-networking.md))* - **LoadBalancer (Service)** — Service type provisioning an external cloud load balancer. *([Ch 18](docs/05-kubernetes/ch18-kubernetes-fundamentals.md))* - **Load shedding** — Rejecting excess work to protect a service. *([Ch 30](docs/05-kubernetes/ch30-service-mesh-istio.md))* - **Load shedding (SRE)** — Rejecting excess traffic quickly to protect core service. *([Ch 34](docs/07-observability-sre/ch34-advanced-sre.md))* - **Load test** — Test with expected normal/high traffic. *([Ch 34](docs/07-observability-sre/ch34-advanced-sre.md))* - **Local route** — Route 10.0.0.0/16 -> local keeping VPC traffic inside the VPC. *([Ch 12](docs/04-aws/ch12-vpc-networking.md))* - **Locals** — Named expressions for reuse inside a module. *([Ch 21](docs/06-iac-config/ch21-terraform.md))* - **Log group** — CloudWatch Logs collection/category of logs. *([Ch 17](docs/04-aws/ch17-monitoring-security.md))* - **Log levels** — DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR severity categories. *([Ch 17](docs/04-aws/ch17-monitoring-security.md))* - **Logs** — Event records answering what happened. *([Ch 22](docs/07-observability-sre/ch22-observability-reliability.md))* - **Log stream** — Sequence of log events from one source within a log group. *([Ch 17](docs/04-aws/ch17-monitoring-security.md))* - **LSI** — Local Secondary Index: same partition key, different sort key. *([Ch 33](docs/04-aws/ch33-advanced-aws-backend.md))*

title: Glossary
heading: M
text: - **MAC address** — Identity of a network interface within a local network segment. *([Ch 4](docs/01-foundations/ch04-networking.md))* - **Macie** — Sensitive-data discovery in S3 (awareness). *([Ch 17](docs/04-aws/ch17-monitoring-security.md))* - **Managed node** — Machine being configured by Ansible. *([Ch 28](docs/06-iac-config/ch28-ansible.md))* - **Managed Node Group** - EKS-managed group of worker nodes. *([Ch 20](docs/05-kubernetes/ch20-kubernetes-networking-scaling.md))* - EKS-managed lifecycle for a group of EC2 worker nodes. *([Ch 31](docs/05-kubernetes/ch31-advanced-eks.md))* - **Matrix strategy** — Runs the same job across multiple configurations (e.g. Node versions). *([Ch 6](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch06-cicd-github-actions.md))* - **maxPods formula** — ENIs x (IPv4 per ENI - 1) + 2 for VPC CNI default mode (supplement). *([Ch 31](docs/05-kubernetes/ch31-advanced-eks.md))* - **Memory ballooning** — Technique where a guest balloon driver allocates memory so the hypervisor can reclaim the corresponding physical pages. *([Ch 36](docs/01-foundations/ch36-virtualization-internals.md))* - **Memory optimized** — Instance family for RAM-heavy workloads. *([Ch 10](docs/04-aws/ch10-ec2-compute.md))* - **Memory overcommitment** — Configuring more total VM memory than physical RAM; managed with ballooning, page sharing, swapping; severe pressure hurts performance. *([Ch 36](docs/01-foundations/ch36-virtualization-internals.md))* - **Merge conflict** — Same lines changed differently in two branches; must be resolved manually. *([Ch 5](docs/01-foundations/ch05-git-github.md))* - **Metric** — Numeric measurement over time. *([Ch 17](docs/04-aws/ch17-monitoring-security.md))* - **Metrics (observability)** — Numeric time-series data answering how much/how often. *([Ch 22](docs/07-observability-sre/ch22-observability-reliability.md))* - **Metrics Server** — Cluster component providing resource metrics for HPA and kubectl top. *([Ch 20](docs/05-kubernetes/ch20-kubernetes-networking-scaling.md))* - **Min / desired / max capacity** — ASG bounds and normal target count. *([Ch 14](docs/04-aws/ch14-load-balancing-scaling.md))* - **Mitigation vs root cause** — Stopping damage now vs understanding why it happened. *([Ch 34](docs/07-observability-sre/ch34-advanced-sre.md))* - **Module (Ansible)** — Reusable unit of automation (apt, copy, service, template...). *([Ch 28](docs/06-iac-config/ch28-ansible.md))* - **Module (Terraform)** — Reusable group of Terraform resources; the root module calls child modules. *([Ch 21](docs/06-iac-config/ch21-terraform.md))* - **Module versioning** — Pinning modules to released versions for controlled promotion. *([Ch 32](docs/06-iac-config/ch32-advanced-terraform.md))* - **Monorepo** — Single repository holding multiple apps/packages (apps/api, apps/worker, packages/shared). *([Ch 35](docs/08-production/ch35-devops-capstone.md))* - **moved block** — Tells Terraform a resource changed address and is not a new resource. *([Ch 32](docs/06-iac-config/ch32-advanced-terraform.md))* - **MTBF** — Mean Time Between Failures (supplement). *([Ch 34](docs/07-observability-sre/ch34-advanced-sre.md))* - **mTLS** — Mutual TLS: both sides authenticate and encrypt traffic. *([Ch 30](docs/05-kubernetes/ch30-service-mesh-istio.md))* - **MTTD** — Mean Time To Detect a problem. *([Ch 34](docs/07-observability-sre/ch34-advanced-sre.md))* - **MTTR** — Mean Time To Recover/Repair/Resolve. *([Ch 34](docs/07-observability-sre/ch34-advanced-sre.md))* - **Multi-AZ (RDS)** — Primary plus standby in another AZ for high availability and failover. *([Ch 13](docs/04-aws/ch13-rds-databases.md))* - **Multi-AZ vs multi-region** — Protect against AZ failure vs regional failure (more complex). *([Ch 34](docs/07-observability-sre/ch34-advanced-sre.md))* - **Multipart upload** — Uploading a large object as separately uploaded parts. *([Ch 11](docs/04-aws/ch11-s3-storage.md))* - **Multi-stage build** — Dockerfile with several FROM stages; only needed output is copied into a small final image. *([Ch 8](docs/02-containers/ch08-docker-production.md))* - **MX record** — DNS mail-exchange record. *([Ch 4](docs/01-foundations/ch04-networking.md))*

title: Glossary
heading: N
text: - **Namespace** — Logical partition of cluster resources. *([Ch 18](docs/05-kubernetes/ch18-kubernetes-fundamentals.md))* - **Namespaces** — Linux kernel feature isolating what a process sees: PID, network, mounts, hostname, users, IPC. *([Ch 36](docs/01-foundations/ch36-virtualization-internals.md))* - **NAT** — Network Address Translation; translates private addresses to public for outbound access. *([Ch 4](docs/01-foundations/ch04-networking.md))* - **NAT Gateway** — Managed NAT allowing private subnets outbound Internet access without inbound reachability. *([Ch 12](docs/04-aws/ch12-vpc-networking.md))* - **needs** — Job keyword creating a dependency on another job. *([Ch 6](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch06-cicd-github-actions.md))* - **Nested paging (EPT / NPT)** — Hardware second-level address translation (Intel EPT, AMD NPT) mapping GPA to HPA, avoiding software shadow tables. *([Ch 36](docs/01-foundations/ch36-virtualization-internals.md))* - **Network** — A collection of devices that can communicate with each other. *([Ch 4](docs/01-foundations/ch04-networking.md))* - **Network ACL (NACL)** — Stateless subnet-level firewall in AWS. *([Ch 4](docs/01-foundations/ch04-networking.md))* - **NetworkPolicy** — Kubernetes rules controlling which Pods/sources may communicate. *([Ch 20](docs/05-kubernetes/ch20-kubernetes-networking-scaling.md))* - **Network segmentation** — Separating tiers with narrow security group rules. *([Ch 17](docs/04-aws/ch17-monitoring-security.md))* - **NLB** — Network Load Balancer: Layer 4 TCP/UDP load balancer. *([Ch 14](docs/04-aws/ch14-load-balancing-scaling.md))* - **Node autoscaling** — Adding/removing worker nodes to match Pod demand. *([Ch 20](docs/05-kubernetes/ch20-kubernetes-networking-scaling.md))* - **Node IAM role** — IAM role attached to the worker node, shared by workloads unless isolated. *([Ch 31](docs/05-kubernetes/ch31-advanced-eks.md))* - **NodePort** — Service type exposing a port on each node. *([Ch 18](docs/05-kubernetes/ch18-kubernetes-fundamentals.md))* - **Noisy neighbor** — One workload consuming shared resources and harming others. *([Ch 34](docs/07-observability-sre/ch34-advanced-sre.md))* - **Non-root container** — Container running the app as an unprivileged user (USER appuser). *([Ch 8](docs/02-containers/ch08-docker-production.md))* - **npm ci** — Clean, lockfile-based install for reproducible CI builds. *([Ch 6](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch06-cicd-github-actions.md))* - **npm ci --omit=dev** — Install production dependencies only. *([Ch 8](docs/02-containers/ch08-docker-production.md))* - **NS record** — DNS name-server record. *([Ch 4](docs/01-foundations/ch04-networking.md))*

title: Glossary
heading: O
text: - **OA (Online Assessment)** — Timed screening test, often MCQ plus coding; this chapter lists high-value DevOps distinctions for it. *([Ch 24](docs/09-interview/ch24-interview-oa-mastery.md))* - **Object key** — The name/path-like identifier of an object within a bucket. *([Ch 11](docs/04-aws/ch11-s3-storage.md))* - **Object (S3)** — Data plus key plus metadata stored in a bucket. *([Ch 11](docs/04-aws/ch11-s3-storage.md))* - **Object storage** — Storage of objects accessed via APIs rather than a mounted filesystem. *([Ch 11](docs/04-aws/ch11-s3-storage.md))* - **Observability** — Ability to understand a system's internal state from external outputs (logs, metrics, traces). *([Ch 22](docs/07-observability-sre/ch22-observability-reliability.md))* - **OIDC (GitHub to AWS)** — Federated identity letting GitHub Actions assume an IAM role with short-lived credentials. *([Ch 9](docs/04-aws/ch09-aws-fundamentals-iam.md))* - **ok/changed/failed/skipped** — Ansible task result states. *([Ch 28](docs/06-iac-config/ch28-ansible.md))* - **On-call** — Rotation of engineers responsible for responding to incidents. *([Ch 34](docs/07-observability-sre/ch34-advanced-sre.md))* - **On-Demand** — Pay-per-use EC2 pricing without commitment. *([Ch 10](docs/04-aws/ch10-ec2-compute.md))* - **On-demand vs provisioned capacity** — DynamoDB automatic vs explicitly specified capacity modes. *([Ch 33](docs/04-aws/ch33-advanced-aws-backend.md))* - **OOMKilled** - Container terminated for exceeding its memory limit. *([Ch 19](docs/05-kubernetes/ch19-kubernetes-config-storage.md))* - Container terminated for exceeding its memory limit (Kubernetes failure table). *([Ch 24](docs/09-interview/ch24-interview-oa-mastery.md))* - **OpenTelemetry (OTel)** — Vendor-neutral framework for traces, metrics and logs. *([Ch 22](docs/07-observability-sre/ch22-observability-reliability.md))* - **OpenTofu** — Open-source fork of Terraform. *([Ch 21](docs/06-iac-config/ch21-terraform.md))* - **Operator** — Controller encoding application-specific operational knowledge (provision, backup, failover, upgrade). *([Ch 29](docs/05-kubernetes/ch29-crds-operators.md))* - **Operator pattern** — Custom Resource plus controller implementing domain automation. *([Ch 29](docs/05-kubernetes/ch29-crds-operators.md))* - **Operator SDK** — Toolkit for building operators. *([Ch 29](docs/05-kubernetes/ch29-crds-operators.md))* - **Option group** — RDS engine-specific additional feature configuration. *([Ch 13](docs/04-aws/ch13-rds-databases.md))* - **Order-processing platform** — Asynchronous API + worker system with PostgreSQL, Redis, SQS and S3. *([Ch 35](docs/08-production/ch35-devops-capstone.md))* - **Order state machine** — PENDING -> PROCESSING -> COMPLETED; FAILED; CANCELLED. *([Ch 35](docs/08-production/ch35-devops-capstone.md))* - **Origin Access Control (OAC)** — CloudFront feature restricting S3 origin access to CloudFront. *([Ch 16](docs/04-aws/ch16-route53-cloudfront-waf.md))* - **Origin (CDN)** — Backend CloudFront fetches from (S3, ALB, EC2). *([Ch 16](docs/04-aws/ch16-route53-cloudfront-waf.md))* - **OSI model** — 7-layer reference model: Application, Presentation, Session, Transport, Network, Data Link, Physical. *([Ch 4](docs/01-foundations/ch04-networking.md))* - **OS-level virtualization** — Isolation provided by the OS kernel (namespaces + cgroups) instead of a hypervisor; the basis of containers. *([Ch 36](docs/01-foundations/ch36-virtualization-internals.md))* - **Outlier detection** — Ejecting unhealthy endpoints from the load-balancing pool (supplement). *([Ch 30](docs/05-kubernetes/ch30-service-mesh-istio.md))* - **OutOfSync** — ArgoCD status: Git desired state differs from cluster. *([Ch 26](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch26-gitops-argocd.md))* - **Output (Terraform)** — Value exposed after apply (terraform output). *([Ch 21](docs/06-iac-config/ch21-terraform.md))* - **Ownership conflict** — Two tools managing the same resource and overwriting each other. *([Ch 32](docs/06-iac-config/ch32-advanced-terraform.md))*

title: Glossary
heading: P
text: - **PaaS** — Platform as a Service: provider manages more; you focus on the application. *([Ch 1](docs/01-foundations/ch01-cloud-devops-fundamentals.md))* - **Packet** — Small unit into which data is broken for transmission. *([Ch 4](docs/01-foundations/ch04-networking.md))* - **Parallel stages** — Independent stages running concurrently to reduce pipeline time. *([Ch 27](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch27-jenkins-advanced-cicd.md))* - **Parameter group** — RDS container for database engine configuration parameters. *([Ch 13](docs/04-aws/ch13-rds-databases.md))* - **Parameter Store** — AWS Systems Manager store for configuration and some secrets. *([Ch 33](docs/04-aws/ch33-advanced-aws-backend.md))* - **Paravirtualization** — Guest uses virtualization-aware drivers instead of full hardware emulation, reducing overhead. *([Ch 36](docs/01-foundations/ch36-virtualization-internals.md))* - **Partition key (PK)** — DynamoDB attribute determining data distribution. *([Ch 33](docs/04-aws/ch33-advanced-aws-backend.md))* - **Path-based routing** — Routing by URL path (e.g. /users/*). *([Ch 14](docs/04-aws/ch14-load-balancing-scaling.md))* - **Path-based routing (Ingress)** — Routing by URL path to different Services. *([Ch 20](docs/05-kubernetes/ch20-kubernetes-networking-scaling.md))* - **PeerAuthentication** — Istio resource configuring mTLS mode (supplement). *([Ch 30](docs/05-kubernetes/ch30-service-mesh-istio.md))* - **Percentile (p95/p99)** — Latency value below which that percent of requests fall. *([Ch 22](docs/07-observability-sre/ch22-observability-reliability.md))* - **PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC)** — Request for storage by an application. *([Ch 19](docs/05-kubernetes/ch19-kubernetes-config-storage.md))* - **PersistentVolume (PV)** — Cluster storage resource independent of Pod lifecycle. *([Ch 19](docs/05-kubernetes/ch19-kubernetes-config-storage.md))* - **PID** — Process ID, unique per process. *([Ch 2](docs/01-foundations/ch02-linux.md))* - **Pilot light** — Minimal standby infrastructure scaled up during disaster. *([Ch 34](docs/07-observability-sre/ch34-advanced-sre.md))* - **Pipe** — `|` feeds the stdout of the left command into the stdin of the right one. *([Ch 3](docs/01-foundations/ch03-bash-automation.md))* - **pipefail** — `set -o pipefail`: a pipeline fails if any command in it fails. *([Ch 3](docs/01-foundations/ch03-bash-automation.md))* - **Pipeline** — Sequence of automated steps from code change to deployment. *([Ch 6](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch06-cicd-github-actions.md))* - **Platform engineering** — Building internal platforms exposing simple APIs (custom resources) over complex infrastructure. *([Ch 29](docs/05-kubernetes/ch29-crds-operators.md))* - **Play** — A mapping of a host group to tasks within a playbook. *([Ch 28](docs/06-iac-config/ch28-ansible.md))* - **Playbook** — YAML file describing desired automation tasks for selected hosts. *([Ch 28](docs/06-iac-config/ch28-ansible.md))* - **Pod** — Smallest deployable unit; one or more tightly coupled containers sharing network/volumes. *([Ch 18](docs/05-kubernetes/ch18-kubernetes-fundamentals.md))* - **PodDisruptionBudget (PDB)** — Limits voluntary disruption of Pods to maintain availability. *([Ch 20](docs/05-kubernetes/ch20-kubernetes-networking-scaling.md))* - **Pod IP exhaustion** — Inability to schedule Pods because no IP addresses are available. *([Ch 31](docs/05-kubernetes/ch31-advanced-eks.md))* - **Pod-level security groups** — Associating AWS security groups with individual Pods. *([Ch 31](docs/05-kubernetes/ch31-advanced-eks.md))* - **Point-in-time recovery (PITR)** — Restoring a database to a chosen moment before an incident. *([Ch 13](docs/04-aws/ch13-rds-databases.md))* - **Policy as code** — Automated rules (OPA, Sentinel) blocking non-compliant infrastructure changes. *([Ch 32](docs/06-iac-config/ch32-advanced-terraform.md))* - **Port** — Number identifying an application/service on a machine. *([Ch 4](docs/01-foundations/ch04-networking.md))* - **port-forward** — kubectl command forwarding a local port to a Pod/Service. *([Ch 18](docs/05-kubernetes/ch18-kubernetes-fundamentals.md))* - **Port mapping (-p)** — `-p HOST_PORT:CONTAINER_PORT` publishes a container port on the host. *([Ch 7](docs/02-containers/ch07-docker-fundamentals.md))* - **post (Jenkins)** — Block defining actions after a pipeline: always, success, failure. *([Ch 27](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch27-jenkins-advanced-cicd.md))* - **Postmortem (blameless)** — Review of an incident focused on systems and processes, not individuals. *([Ch 34](docs/07-observability-sre/ch34-advanced-sre.md))* - **Pre-copy migration** — Live-migration technique that repeatedly copies memory pages changed during the copy until the remainder is small enough to pause and transfer. *([Ch 36](docs/01-foundations/ch36-virtualization-internals.md))* - **Prefix length** — The `/n` in CIDR: number of leading network bits; hosts = 2^(32-n). *([Ch 4](docs/01-foundations/ch04-networking.md))* - **Presigned URL** — Time-limited URL granting temporary access to a specific S3 operation. *([Ch 11](docs/04-aws/ch11-s3-storage.md))* - **prevent_destroy** — Lifecycle setting that errors on plans destroying the resource. *([Ch 32](docs/06-iac-config/ch32-advanced-terraform.md))* - **Principle of least privilege** — Give processes only the permissions they need. *([Ch 8](docs/02-containers/ch08-docker-production.md))* - **Prisma** — TypeScript ORM with schema.prisma and migrations. *([Ch 35](docs/08-production/ch35-devops-capstone.md))* - **Private cloud** — Cloud infrastructure dedicated to one organization. *([Ch 1](docs/01-foundations/ch01-cloud-devops-fundamentals.md))* - **Private hosted zone** — Hosted zone resolving names only inside a VPC. *([Ch 16](docs/04-aws/ch16-route53-cloudfront-waf.md))* - **Private IP** — Address used inside private networks (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16); not routable on the Internet. *([Ch 4](docs/01-foundations/ch04-networking.md))* - **Private subnet** — Subnet with no direct inbound Internet route. *([Ch 4](docs/01-foundations/ch04-networking.md))* - **Privileged instruction** — CPU operation only the kernel/hypervisor may execute (disable interrupts, modify privileged registers, touch hardware); the reason virtualization is hard. *([Ch 36](docs/01-foundations/ch36-virtualization-internals.md))* - **/proc** — Virtual filesystem exposing process and kernel information. *([Ch 2](docs/01-foundations/ch02-linux.md))* - **Process** — A running program. *([Ch 2](docs/01-foundations/ch02-linux.md))* - **prom-client** — Node.js library exposing Prometheus metrics. *([Ch 22](docs/07-observability-sre/ch22-observability-reliability.md))* - **Prometheus** — Metrics monitoring system that scrapes /metrics endpoints. *([Ch 22](docs/07-observability-sre/ch22-observability-reliability.md))* - **Provider lock file** — .terraform.lock.hcl pinning provider versions and checksums; commit it. *([Ch 32](docs/06-iac-config/ch32-advanced-terraform.md))* - **Provider (Terraform)** — Plugin translating Terraform configuration to a platform's APIs (e.g. AWS). *([Ch 21](docs/06-iac-config/ch21-terraform.md))* - **Provisioned concurrency** — Pre-initialized Lambda environments to avoid cold starts. *([Ch 15](docs/04-aws/ch15-lambda-serverless-messaging.md))* - **Prune** — ArgoCD option deleting cluster resources removed from Git. *([Ch 26](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch26-gitops-argocd.md))* - **Public cloud** — Provider-owned infrastructure shared by many isolated customers (AWS, Azure, GCP). *([Ch 1](docs/01-foundations/ch01-cloud-devops-fundamentals.md))* - **Public IP** — Globally routable address. *([Ch 4](docs/01-foundations/ch04-networking.md))* - **Public subnet** — Subnet whose route table has a route to an Internet Gateway. *([Ch 4](docs/01-foundations/ch04-networking.md))* - **Pub/Sub** — Publisher sends to a topic; multiple subscribers receive independently. *([Ch 15](docs/04-aws/ch15-lambda-serverless-messaging.md))* - **Pull** — Fetch plus integrate (merge or rebase). *([Ch 5](docs/01-foundations/ch05-git-github.md))* - **Pull Request** — GitHub collaboration/review mechanism built on branches and commits. *([Ch 5](docs/01-foundations/ch05-git-github.md))*

title: Glossary
heading: Q
text: - **Queue** — Buffer of work between producers and consumers. *([Ch 15](docs/04-aws/ch15-lambda-serverless-messaging.md))* - **Queue depth / queue age** — Number of waiting messages / age of the oldest message. *([Ch 34](docs/07-observability-sre/ch34-advanced-sre.md))* - **QUIC** — UDP-based transport used by HTTP/3. *([Ch 4](docs/01-foundations/ch04-networking.md))*

title: Glossary
heading: R
text: - **Rate-based rule** — WAF rule limiting requests per client over time. *([Ch 16](docs/04-aws/ch16-route53-cloudfront-waf.md))* - **Rate limiting** — Restricting request rate per client/service. *([Ch 22](docs/07-observability-sre/ch22-observability-reliability.md))* - **RBAC** — Role-Based Access Control governing what a ServiceAccount (e.g. an operator) may do. *([Ch 29](docs/05-kubernetes/ch29-crds-operators.md))* - **RDS** — Relational Database Service: AWS-managed relational databases. *([Ch 13](docs/04-aws/ch13-rds-databases.md))* - **RDS Proxy** — Managed connection pooling proxy for RDS. *([Ch 13](docs/04-aws/ch13-rds-databases.md))* - **Read-after-write problem** — Reading stale data from a replica immediately after writing to the primary. *([Ch 13](docs/04-aws/ch13-rds-databases.md))* - **Readiness** — Is the application ready to receive traffic? *([Ch 8](docs/02-containers/ch08-docker-production.md))* - **Readiness endpoint (/ready)** — Check that the app can serve traffic (dependencies reachable). *([Ch 17](docs/04-aws/ch17-monitoring-security.md))* - **Readiness probe** — Check deciding whether a Pod receives traffic. *([Ch 19](docs/05-kubernetes/ch19-kubernetes-config-storage.md))* - **Read replica** — Copy of the database used to scale reads. *([Ch 13](docs/04-aws/ch13-rds-databases.md))* - **ReadWriteOnce** — PVC access mode: read-write by a single node. *([Ch 19](docs/05-kubernetes/ch19-kubernetes-config-storage.md))* - **Rebase** — Replays commits on top of another base, rewriting history to be linear. *([Ch 5](docs/01-foundations/ch05-git-github.md))* - **Rebuild-from-nothing test** — Exercise recreating the entire environment from Terraform, Git and backups. *([Ch 35](docs/08-production/ch35-devops-capstone.md))* - **Reconciliation** — Continuously making actual state match desired state. *([Ch 26](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch26-gitops-argocd.md))* - **Recreate deployment** — Stop old version, start new; simple but downtime. *([Ch 6](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch06-cicd-github-actions.md))* - **Redirection** — Sending streams to files: `>` overwrite, `>>` append, `2>` stderr, `2>&1` merge. *([Ch 3](docs/01-foundations/ch03-bash-automation.md))* - **RED method** — Rate, Errors, Duration for request-driven services. *([Ch 22](docs/07-observability-sre/ch22-observability-reliability.md))* - **Reflog** — Log of where HEAD and branches pointed; used for recovery. *([Ch 5](docs/01-foundations/ch05-git-github.md))* - **Region** — A geographic area containing cloud infrastructure. *([Ch 1](docs/01-foundations/ch01-cloud-devops-fundamentals.md))* - **Registry** — Service storing and distributing images (Docker Hub, GHCR, ECR). *([Ch 7](docs/02-containers/ch07-docker-fundamentals.md))* - **Relative path** — Path relative to the current directory. *([Ch 2](docs/01-foundations/ch02-linux.md))* - **Release (Helm)** — An installed instance of a chart in a cluster. *([Ch 25](docs/05-kubernetes/ch25-helm.md))* - **.Release.Name** — Template object holding the release name. *([Ch 25](docs/05-kubernetes/ch25-helm.md))* - **Reliability** — Whether a system consistently performs correctly over time (distinct from being reachable). *([Ch 1](docs/01-foundations/ch01-cloud-devops-fundamentals.md))* - **Remote** — Reference to another Git repository; `origin` is a conventional name. *([Ch 5](docs/01-foundations/ch05-git-github.md))* - **Remote state / backend** — Shared state storage (e.g. S3) used by teams. *([Ch 21](docs/06-iac-config/ch21-terraform.md))* - **Replicas** — Number of Pod copies desired. *([Ch 18](docs/05-kubernetes/ch18-kubernetes-fundamentals.md))* - **ReplicaSet** — Controller ensuring a set number of identical Pods; managed by Deployments. *([Ch 18](docs/05-kubernetes/ch18-kubernetes-fundamentals.md))* - **Replication lag** — Delay before changes on the primary appear on replicas. *([Ch 13](docs/04-aws/ch13-rds-databases.md))* - **Request ID** — Identifier propagated through logs to correlate one request. *([Ch 22](docs/07-observability-sre/ch22-observability-reliability.md))* - **Reserved / commitment pricing** — Discounted pricing in exchange for committing to usage for a period. *([Ch 10](docs/04-aws/ch10-ec2-compute.md))* - **Reset** — Moves branch pointer (and optionally index/worktree): --soft, --mixed, --hard. *([Ch 5](docs/01-foundations/ch05-git-github.md))* - **Resource limit** — Maximum resources a container may use. *([Ch 19](docs/05-kubernetes/ch19-kubernetes-config-storage.md))* - **Resource request** — Resources reserved/used by the scheduler for placement. *([Ch 19](docs/05-kubernetes/ch19-kubernetes-config-storage.md))* - **Resource (Terraform)** — A managed infrastructure object declared in configuration. *([Ch 21](docs/06-iac-config/ch21-terraform.md))* - **Retry amplification** — Retries multiplying load on an already failing dependency. *([Ch 34](docs/07-observability-sre/ch34-advanced-sre.md))* - **Retry logic** — Application behavior of waiting and retrying when a dependency is unavailable. *([Ch 8](docs/02-containers/ch08-docker-production.md))* - **Retry storm** — Retries amplifying load on an overloaded dependency. *([Ch 22](docs/07-observability-sre/ch22-observability-reliability.md))* - **Reusable workflow** — Central workflow shared by many repositories. *([Ch 6](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch06-cicd-github-actions.md))* - **Reverse proxy** — Proxy in front of servers/applications acting on their behalf (e.g. Nginx). *([Ch 4](docs/01-foundations/ch04-networking.md))* - **Revert** — Creates a new commit that undoes an earlier commit. *([Ch 5](docs/01-foundations/ch05-git-github.md))* - **Ring 0 / Ring 3** — CPU privilege levels: Ring 0 is most privileged (kernel); Ring 3 is least privileged (applications). *([Ch 36](docs/01-foundations/ch36-virtualization-internals.md))* - **Role (Ansible)** — Reusable directory structure of tasks, templates, handlers, variables. *([Ch 28](docs/06-iac-config/ch28-ansible.md))* - **Rollback** - Returning to a previous version after a bad release. *([Ch 6](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch06-cicd-github-actions.md))* - Reverting to a previous version after a bad release. *([Ch 23](docs/08-production/ch23-production-architecture-troubleshooting.md))* - **Roll forward (fix forward)** — Deploy a corrected version instead of reverting. *([Ch 34](docs/07-observability-sre/ch34-advanced-sre.md))* - **Rolling deployment** — Gradually replace instances with new version. *([Ch 6](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch06-cicd-github-actions.md))* - **Rolling deployment (capstone)** — Gradually replace old Pods; failed readiness stalls the rollout. *([Ch 35](docs/08-production/ch35-devops-capstone.md))* - **Rolling update** — Gradual replacement of old Pods with new ones. *([Ch 18](docs/05-kubernetes/ch18-kubernetes-fundamentals.md))* - **rollout restart** — kubectl rollout restart deployment: recreate Pods to pick up changes. *([Ch 19](docs/05-kubernetes/ch19-kubernetes-config-storage.md))* - **rollout undo** — kubectl command rolling a Deployment back to the previous revision. *([Ch 20](docs/05-kubernetes/ch20-kubernetes-networking-scaling.md))* - **Root cause analysis (RCA)** — Investigating the underlying cause after recovery. *([Ch 22](docs/07-observability-sre/ch22-observability-reliability.md))* - **Root module / child module** — Top-level configuration that calls reusable child modules. *([Ch 32](docs/06-iac-config/ch32-advanced-terraform.md))* - **root (user)** — Superuser with extremely broad privileges; home is /root. *([Ch 2](docs/01-foundations/ch02-linux.md))* - **Round robin** — Load-balancing algorithm cycling through servers in order. *([Ch 4](docs/01-foundations/ch04-networking.md))* - **Route 53** — AWS DNS and domain-routing service. *([Ch 16](docs/04-aws/ch16-route53-cloudfront-waf.md))* - **Router** — Device that decides where packets go next. *([Ch 4](docs/01-foundations/ch04-networking.md))* - **Route table** — Rules mapping destination CIDRs to targets (local, igw, NAT). *([Ch 12](docs/04-aws/ch12-vpc-networking.md))* - **Routing table** — Rules mapping destination CIDRs to next hops. *([Ch 4](docs/01-foundations/ch04-networking.md))* - **RPO** — Recovery Point Objective: how much data loss (measured in time) the business can tolerate. *([Ch 1](docs/01-foundations/ch01-cloud-devops-fundamentals.md))* - **RTO** — Recovery Time Objective: how quickly service must be restored after a disaster. *([Ch 1](docs/01-foundations/ch01-cloud-devops-fundamentals.md))* - **run** - Step keyword that executes a shell command. *([Ch 6](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch06-cicd-github-actions.md))* - Dockerfile instruction executed at image build time. *([Ch 7](docs/02-containers/ch07-docker-fundamentals.md))* - **Runbook** — Documented operational procedure for responding to a situation. *([Ch 34](docs/07-observability-sre/ch34-advanced-sre.md))* - **Runner** — The machine/environment (ubuntu-latest etc.) that executes a job. *([Ch 6](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch06-cicd-github-actions.md))* - **Running vs Ready** — A Pod can be running yet not ready to receive traffic. *([Ch 23](docs/08-production/ch23-production-architecture-troubleshooting.md))* - **Runtime (Lambda)** — Language environment for the function (e.g. Node.js). *([Ch 15](docs/04-aws/ch15-lambda-serverless-messaging.md))*

title: Glossary
heading: S
text: - **S3** — Simple Storage Service: scalable object storage accessed via API. *([Ch 11](docs/04-aws/ch11-s3-storage.md))* - **S3 event notification** — Event emitted when objects change, targeting Lambda/SQS/etc. *([Ch 11](docs/04-aws/ch11-s3-storage.md))* - **SaaS** — Software as a Service: finished software you simply use (Gmail, Slack). *([Ch 1](docs/01-foundations/ch01-cloud-devops-fundamentals.md))* - **Saga** — Distributed transaction as local transactions with compensations. *([Ch 33](docs/04-aws/ch33-advanced-aws-backend.md))* - **SAST** — Static Application Security Testing of source code. *([Ch 6](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch06-cicd-github-actions.md))* - **Saved plan** — terraform plan -out file applied exactly with terraform apply. *([Ch 32](docs/06-iac-config/ch32-advanced-terraform.md))* - **Scalability** — Ability of a system to handle increasing workload by adding resources. *([Ch 1](docs/01-foundations/ch01-cloud-devops-fundamentals.md))* - **Scale out / scale in** — Adding / removing instances. *([Ch 14](docs/04-aws/ch14-load-balancing-scaling.md))* - **Scheduled scaling** — Changing capacity at predictable times. *([Ch 14](docs/04-aws/ch14-load-balancing-scaling.md))* - **Scheduler** — Chooses which node runs each Pod. *([Ch 18](docs/05-kubernetes/ch18-kubernetes-fundamentals.md))* - **Scrape** — Prometheus periodically pulling metrics from a target. *([Ch 22](docs/07-observability-sre/ch22-observability-reliability.md))* - **Scripted pipeline** — Free-form Groovy pipeline using node blocks. *([Ch 27](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch27-jenkins-advanced-cicd.md))* - **Sealed Secrets** — Encrypted secrets safe to store in Git, decrypted in-cluster. *([Ch 26](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch26-gitops-argocd.md))* - **Secret (K8s)** — Object holding sensitive data (base64-encoded by default). *([Ch 18](docs/05-kubernetes/ch18-kubernetes-fundamentals.md))* - **secretKeyRef** — Pod env source referencing a single key of a Secret. *([Ch 19](docs/05-kubernetes/ch19-kubernetes-config-storage.md))* - **Secret rotation** — Periodically replacing a secret value (Secrets Manager). *([Ch 17](docs/04-aws/ch17-monitoring-security.md))* - **Secrets Manager** — AWS service for securely storing and retrieving secrets such as DB credentials. *([Ch 13](docs/04-aws/ch13-rds-databases.md))* - **securityContext** — Pod/container security settings (runAsNonRoot, capabilities...). *([Ch 31](docs/05-kubernetes/ch31-advanced-eks.md))* - **Security Group** — Stateful resource-level firewall in AWS. *([Ch 4](docs/01-foundations/ch04-networking.md))* - **Security Group referencing** — Allowing traffic whose source is another security group instead of a CIDR. *([Ch 12](docs/04-aws/ch12-vpc-networking.md))* - **Security Hub** — Aggregated security findings (awareness). *([Ch 17](docs/04-aws/ch17-monitoring-security.md))* - **Selector** — Query matching objects by labels. *([Ch 18](docs/05-kubernetes/ch18-kubernetes-fundamentals.md))* - **Self-heal** — ArgoCD option reverting manual cluster changes to match Git. *([Ch 26](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch26-gitops-argocd.md))* - **Self-healing** — Automatic replacement of failed Pods to match desired replicas. *([Ch 18](docs/05-kubernetes/ch18-kubernetes-fundamentals.md))* - **Self-managed nodes** — Worker nodes whose EC2 lifecycle you manage yourself. *([Ch 31](docs/05-kubernetes/ch31-advanced-eks.md))* - **Sensitive variable** — Variable whose value is hidden in CLI output (still stored in state). *([Ch 32](docs/06-iac-config/ch32-advanced-terraform.md))* - **Serverless** - You do not manage the underlying servers directly (e.g. AWS Lambda). *([Ch 1](docs/01-foundations/ch01-cloud-devops-fundamentals.md))* - You do not manage servers; the provider runs and scales execution. *([Ch 15](docs/04-aws/ch15-lambda-serverless-messaging.md))* - **Service** — Stable network endpoint for a set of Pods. *([Ch 18](docs/05-kubernetes/ch18-kubernetes-fundamentals.md))* - **ServiceAccount** — Kubernetes identity used by Pods. *([Ch 31](docs/05-kubernetes/ch31-advanced-eks.md))* - **Service discovery** — Finding services by stable name (Kubernetes DNS) instead of Pod IPs. *([Ch 20](docs/05-kubernetes/ch20-kubernetes-networking-scaling.md))* - **Service mesh** — Infrastructure layer managing service-to-service communication (traffic, security, reliability, observability). *([Ch 30](docs/05-kubernetes/ch30-service-mesh-istio.md))* - **set -e** — Bash option: exit when a command returns non-zero. *([Ch 3](docs/01-foundations/ch03-bash-automation.md))* - **set -u** — Bash option: error on unset variables. *([Ch 3](docs/01-foundations/ch03-bash-automation.md))* - **SEV levels** — Incident severity classification (SEV-1, SEV-2, SEV-3). *([Ch 34](docs/07-observability-sre/ch34-advanced-sre.md))* - **Shadow page tables** — Older software technique where the hypervisor maintains mappings corresponding to guest page tables; expensive to maintain. *([Ch 36](docs/01-foundations/ch36-virtualization-internals.md))* - **Shared Library (Jenkins)** — Reusable pipeline code shared across repositories (awareness). *([Ch 27](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch27-jenkins-advanced-cicd.md))* - **Shared responsibility model** — AWS secures the cloud; customer secures what they put in the cloud. *([Ch 9](docs/04-aws/ch09-aws-fundamentals-iam.md))* - **Shebang** — First line `#!/bin/bash` naming the interpreter that should execute the script. *([Ch 3](docs/01-foundations/ch03-bash-automation.md))* - **Shell** — Program that takes your commands and passes them to the OS (e.g. bash). *([Ch 2](docs/01-foundations/ch02-linux.md))* - **Sidecar** - Helper container in the same Pod as the main container. *([Ch 18](docs/05-kubernetes/ch18-kubernetes-fundamentals.md))* - Secondary container deployed alongside the application container for cross-cutting functionality. *([Ch 30](docs/05-kubernetes/ch30-service-mesh-istio.md))* - **Sidecar injection** — Automatic addition of the Envoy sidecar to Pods (istio-injection=enabled). *([Ch 30](docs/05-kubernetes/ch30-service-mesh-istio.md))* - **Side-channel attack** — Information leak through shared hardware behaviour (CPU caches, timing, memory behaviour) despite logical isolation. *([Ch 36](docs/01-foundations/ch36-virtualization-internals.md))* - **SIGINT** — Interrupt signal, generated by Ctrl+C. *([Ch 2](docs/01-foundations/ch02-linux.md))* - **SIGKILL** — Signal forcing termination without cleanup (`kill -9`). *([Ch 2](docs/01-foundations/ch02-linux.md))* - **Signed URLs / cookies** — CloudFront mechanism to restrict content to authorized users. *([Ch 16](docs/04-aws/ch16-route53-cloudfront-waf.md))* - **SIGTERM** — Signal requesting graceful termination (default of `kill`). *([Ch 2](docs/01-foundations/ch02-linux.md))* - **Single-table design** — Modeling several entity types in one DynamoDB table. *([Ch 33](docs/04-aws/ch33-advanced-aws-backend.md))* - **SLA** - Service Level Agreement: commitment/expectation about availability or performance. *([Ch 1](docs/01-foundations/ch01-cloud-devops-fundamentals.md))* - Service Level Agreement: formal customer commitment. *([Ch 22](docs/07-observability-sre/ch22-observability-reliability.md))* - **SLI** - Service Level Indicator: a measurement, e.g. successful requests / total requests. *([Ch 1](docs/01-foundations/ch01-cloud-devops-fundamentals.md))* - Service Level Indicator: a measurement. *([Ch 22](docs/07-observability-sre/ch22-observability-reliability.md))* - **SLI types** — Availability, latency, correctness, freshness, durability. *([Ch 34](docs/07-observability-sre/ch34-advanced-sre.md))* - **SLO** - Service Level Objective: a target for an SLI, e.g. 99.9%. *([Ch 1](docs/01-foundations/ch01-cloud-devops-fundamentals.md))* - Service Level Objective: a target for an SLI. *([Ch 22](docs/07-observability-sre/ch22-observability-reliability.md))* - **Snapshot (RDS)** — Explicit point-in-time copy of an RDS database. *([Ch 13](docs/04-aws/ch13-rds-databases.md))* - **Snapshot (VM)** — Captured VM state/storage for later restore or cloning; not a complete backup strategy by itself. *([Ch 36](docs/01-foundations/ch36-virtualization-internals.md))* - **SNS** — Simple Notification Service: managed pub/sub topics. *([Ch 15](docs/04-aws/ch15-lambda-serverless-messaging.md))* - **Soak test** — Long-duration test to find leaks and exhaustion. *([Ch 34](docs/07-observability-sre/ch34-advanced-sre.md))* - **Socket** — IP + port endpoint. *([Ch 4](docs/01-foundations/ch04-networking.md))* - **Sort key (SK)** — DynamoDB attribute ordering items within a partition key. *([Ch 33](docs/04-aws/ch33-advanced-aws-backend.md))* - **Source of truth** — The authoritative place for configuration (Git in GitOps). *([Ch 26](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch26-gitops-argocd.md))* - **Span** — One timed operation within a trace. *([Ch 22](docs/07-observability-sre/ch22-observability-reliability.md))* - **spec** — Section of a resource describing the desired state. *([Ch 29](docs/05-kubernetes/ch29-crds-operators.md))* - **Spike test** — Test with a sudden traffic increase. *([Ch 34](docs/07-observability-sre/ch34-advanced-sre.md))* - **Spot instances** — Discounted spare-capacity instances that can be interrupted. *([Ch 10](docs/04-aws/ch10-ec2-compute.md))* - **SQS** — Simple Queue Service: managed message queue. *([Ch 15](docs/04-aws/ch15-lambda-serverless-messaging.md))* - **SRE** — Site Reliability Engineering: engineering approach to operating reliable production systems. *([Ch 1](docs/01-foundations/ch01-cloud-devops-fundamentals.md))* - **SR-IOV** — PCIe feature letting one physical device expose multiple virtual functions (VF1, VF2, ...) directly to different VMs. *([Ch 36](docs/01-foundations/ch36-virtualization-internals.md))* - **SSE-KMS** — Server-side encryption using AWS KMS keys with extra access control. *([Ch 11](docs/04-aws/ch11-s3-storage.md))* - **SSE-S3** — Server-side encryption with S3-managed keys. *([Ch 11](docs/04-aws/ch11-s3-storage.md))* - **Stage / steps (Jenkins)** — A named phase of a pipeline and the commands inside it. *([Ch 27](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch27-jenkins-advanced-cicd.md))* - **Staging area (index)** — Where you assemble exactly what the next commit contains (`git add`). *([Ch 5](docs/01-foundations/ch05-git-github.md))* - **startupProbe** — Probe protecting slow-starting containers. *([Ch 19](docs/05-kubernetes/ch19-kubernetes-config-storage.md))* - **Stash** — Temporarily stores uncommitted changes. *([Ch 5](docs/01-foundations/ch05-git-github.md))* - **State drift** — Real infrastructure differing from Terraform configuration/state. *([Ch 21](docs/06-iac-config/ch21-terraform.md))* - **Stateful firewall** — Automatically allows return traffic of permitted connections. *([Ch 12](docs/04-aws/ch12-vpc-networking.md))* - **StatefulSet** — Controller for workloads needing stable identity and storage. *([Ch 19](docs/05-kubernetes/ch19-kubernetes-config-storage.md))* - **Stateless API** — API keeping no critical session state locally so any instance can serve any request. *([Ch 10](docs/04-aws/ch10-ec2-compute.md))* - **Stateless architecture** — App servers keep no local session state; shared state is external. *([Ch 14](docs/04-aws/ch14-load-balancing-scaling.md))* - **Stateless container** — Container holding no important state; replaceable freely. *([Ch 7](docs/02-containers/ch07-docker-fundamentals.md))* - **Stateless firewall** — Evaluates inbound and outbound rules independently (NACL). *([Ch 12](docs/04-aws/ch12-vpc-networking.md))* - **State locking** — Preventing concurrent operations from corrupting state. *([Ch 21](docs/06-iac-config/ch21-terraform.md))* - **State machine** — Workflow of states and transitions (Step Functions). *([Ch 33](docs/04-aws/ch33-advanced-aws-backend.md))* - **status** — Section of a resource describing the observed/current state. *([Ch 29](docs/05-kubernetes/ch29-crds-operators.md))* - **stderr** — Standard error stream (error output); redirect with `2>`. *([Ch 3](docs/01-foundations/ch03-bash-automation.md))* - **stdin** — Standard input stream of a process. *([Ch 3](docs/01-foundations/ch03-bash-automation.md))* - **stdout** — Standard output stream (normal output). *([Ch 3](docs/01-foundations/ch03-bash-automation.md))* - **Step** — One operation inside a job (a `run` command or a `uses` action). *([Ch 6](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch06-cicd-github-actions.md))* - **Step Functions** - AWS workflow orchestration service (awareness). *([Ch 15](docs/04-aws/ch15-lambda-serverless-messaging.md))* - Workflow orchestration using state machines. *([Ch 33](docs/04-aws/ch33-advanced-aws-backend.md))* - **Step scaling** — Add capacity in steps according to metric thresholds. *([Ch 14](docs/04-aws/ch14-load-balancing-scaling.md))* - **Sticky sessions** — Load balancer sending a user's requests to the same target. *([Ch 14](docs/04-aws/ch14-load-balancing-scaling.md))* - **Stop vs terminate (EC2)** — Stop can be restarted; terminate deletes the instance. *([Ch 10](docs/04-aws/ch10-ec2-compute.md))* - **Storage class** — S3 tier optimized for an access pattern (Standard, Standard-IA, Glacier...). *([Ch 11](docs/04-aws/ch11-s3-storage.md))* - **StorageClass** — Describes how storage is dynamically provisioned. *([Ch 19](docs/05-kubernetes/ch19-kubernetes-config-storage.md))* - **Storage optimized** — Instance family for high local storage performance. *([Ch 10](docs/04-aws/ch10-ec2-compute.md))* - **Stress test** — Test beyond expected capacity until degradation. *([Ch 34](docs/07-observability-sre/ch34-advanced-sre.md))* - **Structured logging** — Logging machine-readable (JSON) events with consistent fields. *([Ch 17](docs/04-aws/ch17-monitoring-security.md))* - **STS** — Security Token Service issuing temporary credentials; `aws sts get-caller-identity`. *([Ch 9](docs/04-aws/ch09-aws-fundamentals-iam.md))* - **Subnet** — Subdivision of a VPC CIDR range that lives in a single AZ. *([Ch 12](docs/04-aws/ch12-vpc-networking.md))* - **Subnetting** — Dividing a network into smaller segments. *([Ch 4](docs/01-foundations/ch04-networking.md))* - **Subset** — Named group of Pods (by labels) addressed by a DestinationRule. *([Ch 30](docs/05-kubernetes/ch30-service-mesh-istio.md))* - **sudo** — Run a command with elevated privileges, subject to the user's sudo permissions. *([Ch 2](docs/01-foundations/ch02-linux.md))* - **Supply-chain security** — Protecting build/deploy tooling and artifacts from compromise. *([Ch 27](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch27-jenkins-advanced-cicd.md))* - **Sync (ArgoCD)** — Applying the Git-defined state to the cluster. *([Ch 26](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch26-gitops-argocd.md))* - **Synced** — ArgoCD status: cluster matches Git. *([Ch 26](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch26-gitops-argocd.md))* - **systemd** — Init/service manager on modern Linux; controlled with systemctl. *([Ch 2](docs/01-foundations/ch02-linux.md))* - **Systems Manager Session Manager** — Shell access to instances without opening public SSH. *([Ch 10](docs/04-aws/ch10-ec2-compute.md))*

title: Glossary
heading: T
text: - **Tag** — Named marker for an important point (release), e.g. v1.0.0. *([Ch 5](docs/01-foundations/ch05-git-github.md))* - **Tags (Ansible)** — Labels to run only selected tasks. *([Ch 28](docs/06-iac-config/ch28-ansible.md))* - **Tail latency** — Latency of the slowest requests (p95, p99, p99.9). *([Ch 34](docs/07-observability-sre/ch34-advanced-sre.md))* - **tar** — Archiving tool; `-czf` create gzip archive, `-xzf` extract. *([Ch 3](docs/01-foundations/ch03-bash-automation.md))* - **Target group** — Set of backend targets (instances, IPs, containers) an ALB routes to. *([Ch 14](docs/04-aws/ch14-load-balancing-scaling.md))* - **Target tracking scaling** — Keep a metric near a target (e.g. CPU 50%). *([Ch 14](docs/04-aws/ch14-load-balancing-scaling.md))* - **Target type (instance vs IP)** — Whether the load balancer targets nodes or Pod IPs directly. *([Ch 31](docs/05-kubernetes/ch31-advanced-eks.md))* - **Task (Ansible)** — One unit of work calling a module. *([Ch 28](docs/06-iac-config/ch28-ansible.md))* - **Task definition** — ECS blueprint: image, CPU, memory, ports, environment, roles, logging. *([Ch 33](docs/04-aws/ch33-advanced-aws-backend.md))* - **Task role vs task execution role** — App's AWS permissions vs ECS's permissions to pull images/write logs. *([Ch 33](docs/04-aws/ch33-advanced-aws-backend.md))* - **TCP** — Transmission Control Protocol: reliable, ordered byte-stream transport. *([Ch 4](docs/01-foundations/ch04-networking.md))* - **TCP/IP model** — 4-layer practical model: Application, Transport, Internet, Network Access. *([Ch 4](docs/01-foundations/ch04-networking.md))* - **Template (Ansible/Jinja2)** — File rendered with variables, e.g. app.conf.j2. *([Ch 28](docs/06-iac-config/ch28-ansible.md))* - **Terraform** — Infrastructure as Code tool for declaratively creating and managing infrastructure. *([Ch 21](docs/06-iac-config/ch21-terraform.md))* - **terraform apply** — Apply planned changes via provider APIs. *([Ch 21](docs/06-iac-config/ch21-terraform.md))* - **terraform destroy** — Destroy all resources managed by the configuration. *([Ch 21](docs/06-iac-config/ch21-terraform.md))* - **terraform import** — Adopt an existing resource into state. *([Ch 21](docs/06-iac-config/ch21-terraform.md))* - **terraform init** — Initialize working directory and download providers. *([Ch 21](docs/06-iac-config/ch21-terraform.md))* - **.terraform.lock.hcl** — Dependency lock file for provider versions/checksums; commit it. *([Ch 21](docs/06-iac-config/ch21-terraform.md))* - **terraform plan** — Preview changes between configuration and known/real state. *([Ch 21](docs/06-iac-config/ch21-terraform.md))* - **terraform_remote_state** — Data source reading outputs from another state. *([Ch 32](docs/06-iac-config/ch32-advanced-terraform.md))* - **Terraform required_version** — Constraint on which Terraform CLI versions may run the configuration. *([Ch 32](docs/06-iac-config/ch32-advanced-terraform.md))* - **Terraform state** — File (terraform.tfstate) mapping configuration to real infrastructure. *([Ch 21](docs/06-iac-config/ch21-terraform.md))* - **terraform state list/show** — List or inspect resources tracked in state. *([Ch 32](docs/06-iac-config/ch32-advanced-terraform.md))* - **terraform state rm** — Removes a resource from state without deleting the real resource. *([Ch 32](docs/06-iac-config/ch32-advanced-terraform.md))* - **Terraform workspace** — Separate state instance for the same configuration. *([Ch 32](docs/06-iac-config/ch32-advanced-terraform.md))* - **Three-tier architecture** — Presentation, application and data tiers in separate network layers. *([Ch 12](docs/04-aws/ch12-vpc-networking.md))* - **Three-tier production architecture** — Edge (DNS/CDN/WAF/LB) -> application (EKS Pods) -> data (RDS/Redis/S3). *([Ch 23](docs/08-production/ch23-production-architecture-troubleshooting.md))* - **Three-way handshake** — SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK sequence establishing a TCP connection. *([Ch 4](docs/01-foundations/ch04-networking.md))* - **Three-way merge** — Merge using the common ancestor and both branch tips; usually creates a merge commit. *([Ch 5](docs/01-foundations/ch05-git-github.md))* - **Timeout** — Maximum time to wait for a call before failing. *([Ch 22](docs/07-observability-sre/ch22-observability-reliability.md))* - **Timeout budget** — Overall time allowance divided across calls in a request path. *([Ch 30](docs/05-kubernetes/ch30-service-mesh-istio.md))* - **TLB (Translation Lookaside Buffer)** — CPU cache of recent address translations that avoids repeated page-table walks. *([Ch 36](docs/01-foundations/ch36-virtualization-internals.md))* - **TLS** — Transport Layer Security: confidentiality, integrity, server authentication. *([Ch 4](docs/01-foundations/ch04-networking.md))* - **TLS termination** — Decrypting TLS at a load balancer, reverse proxy or CDN. *([Ch 4](docs/01-foundations/ch04-networking.md))* - **Token bucket** — Rate-limiting algorithm allowing bursts with a refill rate. *([Ch 34](docs/07-observability-sre/ch34-advanced-sre.md))* - **Trace ID** — Identifier shared by all spans of one request. *([Ch 22](docs/07-observability-sre/ch22-observability-reliability.md))* - **Traces** — Records of a single request's path and time across services. *([Ch 22](docs/07-observability-sre/ch22-observability-reliability.md))* - **Transactional outbox** — Writing events to a DB table in the same transaction, then publishing them reliably. *([Ch 33](docs/04-aws/ch33-advanced-aws-backend.md))* - **Trigger (on)** — Event that starts a workflow (push, pull_request, ...). *([Ch 6](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch06-cicd-github-actions.md))* - **Trunk-based development** — Frequent integration of small changes into main/trunk using short-lived branches. *([Ch 5](docs/01-foundations/ch05-git-github.md))* - **TTL** — Time To Live: how long resolvers may cache a DNS answer. *([Ch 16](docs/04-aws/ch16-route53-cloudfront-waf.md))* - **TXT record** — DNS record with arbitrary text (verification etc.). *([Ch 4](docs/01-foundations/ch04-networking.md))* - **Type 1 hypervisor (bare-metal)** — Hypervisor that runs directly on hardware (e.g. VMware ESXi, Hyper-V, Xen, KVM-based environments); common in data centers. *([Ch 36](docs/01-foundations/ch36-virtualization-internals.md))* - **Type 2 hypervisor** — Hypervisor that runs as an application on a host OS (e.g. VirtualBox, VMware Workstation, Parallels); convenient for desktop development. *([Ch 36](docs/01-foundations/ch36-virtualization-internals.md))* - **Type check** — tsc --noEmit: verify TypeScript types without producing output. *([Ch 6](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch06-cicd-github-actions.md))*

title: Glossary
heading: U
text: - **UDP** — User Datagram Protocol: connectionless, no delivery guarantee, low overhead. *([Ch 4](docs/01-foundations/ch04-networking.md))* - **Unit / Integration / E2E tests** — Small pieces / multiple components together / whole system from user view. *([Ch 6](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch06-cicd-github-actions.md))* - **Upstream** — Conventional remote name for the original repository of a fork. *([Ch 5](docs/01-foundations/ch05-git-github.md))* - **User data** — Script executed at instance launch for bootstrapping. *([Ch 10](docs/04-aws/ch10-ec2-compute.md))* - **uses** — Step keyword that runs an existing Action (e.g. actions/checkout@v4). *([Ch 6](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch06-cicd-github-actions.md))*

title: Glossary
heading: V
text: - **.Values** — Template object exposing values supplied to the chart. *([Ch 25](docs/05-kubernetes/ch25-helm.md))* - **Values precedence** — Defaults < values files < --set; the most specific override wins. *([Ch 25](docs/05-kubernetes/ch25-helm.md))* - **values.yaml** — Default configuration values of a Helm chart. *([Ch 25](docs/05-kubernetes/ch25-helm.md))* - **Variable (Terraform)** — Input parameter of a configuration (var.name). *([Ch 21](docs/06-iac-config/ch21-terraform.md))* - **Vault** — HashiCorp secrets-management system. *([Ch 26](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch26-gitops-argocd.md))* - **vCPU** — Virtual CPU: an execution context scheduled by the hypervisor onto physical CPUs; not necessarily a dedicated physical core. *([Ch 36](docs/01-foundations/ch36-virtualization-internals.md))* - **Versioning** — Keeping multiple versions of an S3 object. *([Ch 11](docs/04-aws/ch11-s3-storage.md))* - **Vertical scaling (scale up)** — Making one machine more powerful (more CPU/RAM). *([Ch 1](docs/01-foundations/ch01-cloud-devops-fundamentals.md))* - **VirtIO** — Common paravirtualized driver standard for virtual network and block devices in Linux virtualization. *([Ch 36](docs/01-foundations/ch36-virtualization-internals.md))* - **Virtual disk (VMDK / VHDX / QCOW2 / raw)** — File or volume format that backs a VM's disk as an abstraction over underlying storage. *([Ch 36](docs/01-foundations/ch36-virtualization-internals.md))* - **Virtualization** — Creating an abstraction of physical computing resources so multiple isolated virtual machines can share physical hardware. *([Ch 36](docs/01-foundations/ch36-virtualization-internals.md))* - **Virtual NIC** — Virtual network interface (with MAC/IP) presented to the guest and forwarded by the hypervisor. *([Ch 36](docs/01-foundations/ch36-virtualization-internals.md))* - **VirtualService** — Istio resource defining traffic routing rules. *([Ch 30](docs/05-kubernetes/ch30-service-mesh-istio.md))* - **Virtual switch** — Hypervisor-provided switch connecting VMs and the physical NIC; can do switching, VLANs, filtering, bridging. *([Ch 36](docs/01-foundations/ch36-virtualization-internals.md))* - **Visibility timeout** — Time an SQS message stays hidden after being received. *([Ch 15](docs/04-aws/ch15-lambda-serverless-messaging.md))* - **VM escape** — Attack in which code in a guest breaks out through a hypervisor vulnerability to the host and possibly other VMs. *([Ch 36](docs/01-foundations/ch36-virtualization-internals.md))* - **VM exit** — Transition from guest execution into the hypervisor when an operation needs hypervisor handling; has overhead, so frequent exits hurt performance. *([Ch 36](docs/01-foundations/ch36-virtualization-internals.md))* - **VM isolation** — Separation of CPU, memory, storage, network and devices between VMs; the hypervisor is a critical security boundary. *([Ch 36](docs/01-foundations/ch36-virtualization-internals.md))* - **Volume (Docker)** — Docker-managed persistent storage independent of container lifecycle. *([Ch 7](docs/02-containers/ch07-docker-fundamentals.md))* - **Volume (Kubernetes)** — Storage attached to a Pod and mounted into containers. *([Ch 19](docs/05-kubernetes/ch19-kubernetes-config-storage.md))* - **volumeMount** — Mounting a volume at a path inside a container. *([Ch 19](docs/05-kubernetes/ch19-kubernetes-config-storage.md))* - **VPC** — Virtual Private Cloud: logically isolated AWS network. *([Ch 9](docs/04-aws/ch09-aws-fundamentals-iam.md))* - **VPC endpoint** — Private connectivity from a VPC to supported AWS services. *([Ch 12](docs/04-aws/ch12-vpc-networking.md))* - **VPC Flow Logs** — Logs of IP traffic to/from network interfaces. *([Ch 12](docs/04-aws/ch12-vpc-networking.md))*

title: Glossary
heading: W
text: - **WAF** — Web Application Firewall filtering HTTP requests (SQLi, XSS, bots, rate limits). *([Ch 16](docs/04-aws/ch16-route53-cloudfront-waf.md))* - **Warm standby** — Reduced-capacity running copy scaled up during disaster. *([Ch 34](docs/07-observability-sre/ch34-advanced-sre.md))* - **Web ACL** — Collection of WAF rules associated with a CloudFront distribution or ALB. *([Ch 16](docs/04-aws/ch16-route53-cloudfront-waf.md))* - **Webhook** — HTTP callback sent by GitHub to trigger a Jenkins pipeline. *([Ch 27](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch27-jenkins-advanced-cicd.md))* - **Weighted load balancing** — Algorithm giving servers different traffic shares. *([Ch 4](docs/01-foundations/ch04-networking.md))* - **Well-Architected Framework** — AWS design pillars: operational excellence, security, reliability, performance, cost, sustainability. *([Ch 33](docs/04-aws/ch33-advanced-aws-backend.md))* - **withCredentials** — Pipeline step exposing a credential to commands as a variable. *([Ch 27](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch27-jenkins-advanced-cicd.md))* - **WORKDIR** — Dockerfile instruction setting the working directory. *([Ch 7](docs/02-containers/ch07-docker-fundamentals.md))* - **Worker idempotency** — Processing each eventId at most once effectively by recording processed events. *([Ch 35](docs/08-production/ch35-devops-capstone.md))* - **Worker node** — Machine that runs workloads (kubelet, runtime, Pods). *([Ch 18](docs/05-kubernetes/ch18-kubernetes-fundamentals.md))* - **Workflow** — A YAML-defined automated process in GitHub Actions containing one or more jobs. *([Ch 6](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch06-cicd-github-actions.md))* - **Working directory (working tree)** — Your actual project files on disk. *([Ch 5](docs/01-foundations/ch05-git-github.md))* - **Workload identity** — Giving Pods AWS permissions via IAM identity instead of static keys (IRSA / Pod Identity). *([Ch 20](docs/05-kubernetes/ch20-kubernetes-networking-scaling.md))* - **Workspace (Terraform)** — Separate state instances within one configuration. *([Ch 21](docs/06-iac-config/ch21-terraform.md))*

title: Glossary
heading: X
text: - **xargs** — Turns input lines into command arguments. *([Ch 3](docs/01-foundations/ch03-bash-automation.md))*

title: Glossary
heading: Z
text: - **Zero trust** — Security model not trusting network location; requires identity, authentication, authorization and encryption. *([Ch 30](docs/05-kubernetes/ch30-service-mesh-istio.md))*

title: Corrections
heading: Corrections, Clarifications and Verify-Items
text: This is the curated list of places where the source material is **technically wrong, imprecise, incomplete, internally inconsistent or time-sensitive**. The unabridged working log (including minor notes) is [docs/00-start-here/corrections-log-by-chapter.md](docs/00-start-here/corrections-log-by-chapter.md).

title: Corrections
heading: Policy
text: - **Source text is never silently changed.** Imported chapter text is identical to the source apart from the documented mechanical transformations (see [AUDIT_REPORT.md](AUDIT_REPORT.md)). A correction lives *beside* the text — here, in the chapter's revision sheet, or in its clearly labelled "Editorial supplement". - **Status legend** - **Verified** — checked against a primary source (official documentation page) *in this project*; the page is named. - **Reference** — the cited official documentation is the right place to confirm, but it was **not** re-fetched here. Treat as "believed correct; confirm before relying on it". - **Verify at use time** — depends on a version, price, quota or date and may already have changed. - Nothing is marked *Verified* without a fetched source. "Reference" items are honest pointers, not claims of independent confirmation. ---

title: Corrections
heading: A. Technical corrections (the source is wrong or misleading as written)
text: | # | Chapter | Issue | Correct statement | Status / reference | |---|---|---|---|---| | A1 | [26](docs/03-cicd-gitops/ch26-gitops-argocd.md) (§25, §37) | Says automated sync lets ArgoCD "reconcile the cluster back" after manual changes. | `syncPolicy.automated` alone does **not** revert live-cluster edits; the app shows *OutOfSync*. Reverting needs `selfHeal: true`; deleting resources removed from Git needs `prune: true`. Both default to **false**. | **Verified** — Argo CD docs, *Automated Sync Policy* (argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/user-guide/auto_sync/) | | A2 | [21](docs/06-iac-config/ch21-terraform.md) (§24) | `aws_instance` example uses `security_groups = [aws_security_group.app.name]`. | For an instance in a non-default VPC subnet use `vpc_security_group_ids = [aws_security_group.app.id]`. | Reference — Terraform AWS provider docs, `aws_instance` | | A3 | [28](docs/06-iac-config/ch28-ansible.md) (§25–26) | Uses a play variable named `environment`. | `environment` is an Ansible **keyword** (task/play environment variables); pick another name such as `app_env`. | Reference — Ansible docs, *Creating valid variable names* / *Playbook keywords* | | A4 | [3](docs/01-foundations/ch03-bash-automation.md) (§21) | `ps aux \| grep node \| wc -l` as a process count. | It also counts the `grep` itself (off by one). Use `pgrep -c node` or `grep [n]ode`. | Reference — procps/GNU grep behaviour | | A5 | [33](docs/04-aws/ch33-advanced-aws-backend.md) (§34) | `redis.set(key, value, { EX: 300 })`. | That is **node-redis v4** syntax; **ioredis** (used in Chapter 35) takes positional arguments: `set(key, value, "EX", 300)`. | Reference — library docs | | A6 | [32](docs/06-iac-config/ch32-advanced-terraform.md) (§55, §56, §85) | `required_version = ">= 1.x, < 2.0"`, `source = "..."`, `for_each = { api = "..." }`. | Placeholders, not valid HCL. Valid forms are in the chapter's supplement. | Editorial | | A7 | [32](docs/06-iac-config/ch32-advanced-terraform.md) (§4) | First `.gitignore` lists `.terraform.lock.hcl`. | The source corrects itself immediately: **commit** the lock file. Final advice agrees with Chapter 21 §19. | Source self-correction |

title: Corrections
heading: B. Precision issues (true in spirit, misleading if memorised literally)
text: | # | Chapter | Statement | More precise | |---|---|---|---| | B1 | [1](docs/01-foundations/ch01-cloud-devops-fundamentals.md) (§22) | SLA = "commitment/expectation". | An SLA is **contractual** with consequences (credits/penalties); the SLO is the internal target. Chapter 34 uses the precise definition. | | B2 | [4](docs/01-foundations/ch04-networking.md) (§11) | A `/24` has 254 usable hosts. | Traditional figure. **AWS reserves 5 addresses per subnet → 251 usable.** (Reference: AWS VPC User Guide, *Subnet CIDR blocks*) | | B3 | [4](docs/01-foundations/ch04-networking.md) (§19) | DNS "commonly UDP". | Also TCP (large responses, zone transfers) and DNS-over-TLS/HTTPS. | | B4 | [14](docs/04-aws/ch14-load-balancing-scaling.md) (§40) | "ASG can also use health information". | By default an ASG uses **EC2 status checks**; enable ELB health checks on the ASG so a failing ALB target is replaced. (Reference: EC2 Auto Scaling User Guide, *Health checks*) | | B5 | [18](docs/05-kubernetes/ch18-kubernetes-fundamentals.md) (§51) | Lists `CrashLoopBackOff`/`ImagePullBackOff` with Pod phases. | Those are container-status **reasons**; Pod phases are Pending, Running, Succeeded, Failed, Unknown. | | B6 | [16](docs/04-aws/ch16-route53-cloudfront-waf.md) (§35, 36, 44) | WAF drawn as a hop in the traffic path. | WAF is **attached** to CloudFront/ALB (a web ACL association), not a separate hop.
